meaning: Start a line with ! inside Claude to run a shell command yourself; its output lands in the conversation.
In Markdown, # plus a space starts a heading. In shell scripts and terminal examples, text after # is a note for humans that is ignored.
The first line of a script, like #!/bin/bash, telling the computer which program runs the script.
Shown before a command as the terminal prompt (don't type it). Inside commands, $ reads a variable's value, like $CMD.
$( ... ) runs the command inside the brackets and uses its output as a value, e.g. CMD=$(jq ...).
In a shell script, the first argument given to it. Run ./review.sh 42 and $1 is 42.
In a custom command or skill file, a placeholder replaced by whatever you type after the command name.
The $ reads the value of CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: the path to your project folder. Used in hook commands to point at scripts inside the project.
Reads the value stored in the CMD variable: here, the shell command Claude is about to run.
In GitHub workflow files, ${{ ... }} inserts a value, like ${{ secrets.NAME }} which inserts a stored secret without writing it in the file.
Joins two commands: run the second only if the first succeeded.
Matches anything. Bash(npm run *) matches any command that starts with npm run.
In file patterns: any files in any subfolder, at any depth. Read(./docs/**) covers everything inside docs.
With chmod: lets the file be run as a program.
On its own, it means 'end of options': everything after it belongs to the command that follows, not to claude. E.g. claude mcp add name -- npx ...
Three dashes on their own line mark the start and end of the YAML frontmatter block at the top of a Markdown file.
With git log: show only the last 20 commits.
With git worktree add: create a new branch with the name that follows, e.g. -b feature-a.
With claude: reopen your most recent conversation in this folder.
With claude mcp add: pass a setting (environment variable) to the server, written KEY=value.
A placeholder showing the short form of a flag: one dash and one letter, versus two dashes and a word for the long form.
Four curl options together: fail on server errors, stay silent, but still show errors, and follow redirects. Common in install commands.
With npm install: install the program for your whole computer, so the command works in every folder.
With claude: answer one prompt, print the result and exit (headless mode). With mkdir: also create any missing parent folders.
With grep: print nothing, just report whether a match was found.
With claude: open a picker of past sessions, or a specific one by ID. With jq: print raw text without quotes. With pnpm: run in every package of the project (recursive).
With rm: -r (recursive) deletes folders and everything inside, -f (force) never asks. rm -rf deletes permanently with no confirmation.
With claude mcp add: choose how Claude connects to the server (http, stdio or sse).
With claude: start in a new isolated worktree (a separate working copy of the repo).
The folder one level up (the parent folder). cd .. moves up one level.
Start of a path in the parent folder, e.g. ../project-feature-a is a sibling folder.
The current folder, at the start of a path. In permission rules it means the project folder; ./review.sh runs a script from here.
A hidden folder (the dot hides it) holding Claude Code settings, commands, skills, agents and hooks.
A file that controls how a web page looks: colors, sizes, layout.
A file that holds secret settings like passwords and API keys. It should never be shared or read by tools that don't need it.
A JavaScript code file.
A JSON file: structured data in { } and [ ]. Claude Code settings live in .json files.
A log file: a record of what a program printed while it ran.
The project file that lists MCP servers shared with the team (project scope).
A Markdown file: plain text with simple formatting like # for headings. CLAUDE.md and SKILL.md are Markdown.
A Python code file.
A shell script: a text file of terminal commands run in order.
A TypeScript code file. TypeScript is JavaScript with labels for what kind of data each value holds.
A TypeScript file that also describes screen parts (components) using HTML-like tags, common in React apps.
A plain text file.
A YAML settings file, like docker-compose.yml or a GitHub workflow.
Sends error messages (stderr) into the same stream as normal output, so a pipe captures both.
With chmod: a number code meaning you can read, write and run the file, and everyone else can read and run it.
An older way to write a wildcard at the end of a command rule: Bash(ls:*) means the same as Bash(ls *).
< file feeds a file into a command as its input. In patterns like <name>, the angle brackets mark a placeholder you replace.
After a command, > file saves the output into that file. At the start of a line, > is just the prompt where you type inside a Claude session.
Sends what echo prints to stderr (the error channel) instead of normal output. In a hook, that text is shown to Claude as the reason.
In a Claude prompt, @ points at a file or folder so Claude reads it, e.g. @src/app.ts. In package names it marks an owner or version.
Asks for the newest version of a package, e.g. npx @playwright/mcp@latest.
In a GitHub workflow, picks version 1 of an action, e.g. anthropics/claude-code-action@v1.
Software that can understand and produce language, images or decisions in a human-like way. Claude is an AI.
The name of the setting (environment variable) that holds your secret Anthropic API key, the password that lets a program use Claude on your account.
A fixed set of requests one program can send to another to get data or make it do something. A web app's API is how other code talks to it.
Plural of API: fixed sets of requests programs use to talk to each other.
The extra words given to a command that tell it what to work on. In MCP settings, "args" lists them for the server's launch command.
Part of $ARGUMENTS, the placeholder for what you type after a custom command's name.
Checking who a user is, such as logging in. gh auth login signs you in to GitHub.
Amazon's cloud platform, and its command-line tool.
Claude's built-in tool for running terminal commands. Permission rules like Bash(npm test) control which commands it may run.
A common shell: the program that reads and runs what you type in a terminal. 'Bash mode' (!) runs a command yourself inside Claude.
Homebrew, a popular tool for installing programs on a Mac from the terminal.
Writing joined words with each new word capitalized except the first, like acceptEdits. Claude Code values must match this exactly.
A command that prints a file's contents, e.g. cat logs.txt.
A command that moves you into another folder. cd .. goes up one level.
A command that changes a file's permissions, e.g. chmod +x lets a script run.
An automatic system that runs your tests and checks every time code is pushed, without a person starting it. GitHub Actions is one example.
A setting (environment variable) Claude Code fills in with the path of your project folder, so hook scripts can find files no matter where they run.
A program you control by typing commands in a terminal instead of clicking buttons. Claude Code and gh are CLIs.
A variable name chosen in the example hook script to hold the command Claude wants to run. $CMD reads its value.
A script that writes code automatically from another source; generated files shouldn't be edited by hand.
Settings that control how a program behaves.
A command that copies a file.
A simple spreadsheet file format: plain text where each line is a row and commas separate the columns.
The Control key. Ctrl+C means hold Control and press C.
A command that downloads or sends data to a web address from the terminal.
Short for database: an organized store of data an app reads from and writes to.
Short for database. In the content it is also used as a name, like the db MCP server or the db service in docker compose.
The version of an app you run on your own machine while building it, e.g. npm run dev starts the dev server.
A view of exactly what changed in files: removed lines and added lines. git diff shows your uncommitted changes.
Another word for folder.
Means 'for example'.
A command that prints the text you give it.
The Escape key, top-left on most keyboards. In Claude Code it stops Claude mid-turn; pressing it twice opens the rewind menu.
Closes an if block in a shell script ('if' spelled backwards).
A settings block at the top of a Markdown file, between two --- lines, written as key: value pairs.
An old way to move files between computers. Not an MCP transport.
The type of web request that asks a server to send data back, like loading a page. GET /users means 'fetch the list of users'.
GitHub's official command-line tool, used for things like opening pull requests (gh pr create).
The version-control tool that tracks every change to your project's files, so you can review, save (commit) and undo work.
Claude's built-in tool for finding files by name pattern, like every .ts file (a 'glob' is a pattern with wildcards such as *).
A way for apps to ask a server for exactly the data they need in one request, an alternative to REST.
Claude's built-in tool for searching inside files for text, named after the grep command.
A command that searches text for a pattern. Also the name of Claude's built-in search tool, Grep.
The basic set of rules browsers and servers use to send data over the web. For MCP, HTTP is the recommended way to connect to remote servers.
Lowercase spelling used as a value, like --transport http: connect to a remote MCP server over the web. Also the start of web addresses.
The secure, encrypted version of http, seen at the start of web addresses like https://claude.ai.
A unique code that names one specific thing, like the ID of a past session you can pass to --resume.
Short for IP address: the number that identifies a device on the internet. 'Per IP' means counted separately for each visitor's device.
A small command-line tool for reading JSON and pulling out fields, e.g. jq -r '.result'.
A programming language that runs websites and many tools. Files end in .js.
A plain-text format for structured data: { } holds key/value pairs and [ ] holds lists. Claude Code's settings files are JSON.
Lowercase spelling used as a value, like --output-format json: give the answer as structured JSON data instead of plain text.
A unit of file size, about a thousand characters of text.
The pattern for setting an environment variable: a name, an equals sign, and its value.
Automatically checking code for style problems and likely mistakes. A linter is the tool that does it.
A file (like package-lock.json) that records the exact version of every installed package. It is generated, not edited by hand.
A command that lists the files and folders in the current folder.
An open standard that lets Claude plug into outside tools and data, like GitHub, a browser or a database.
Lowercase spelling used in commands like claude mcp add, which manages MCP connections.
The start of every MCP tool's name, in the pattern mcp__<server>__<tool>, e.g. mcp__github__create_issue. The double underscores separate the parts.
A command that creates a new folder. mkdir -p also creates any missing parent folders.
One repository holding several related projects or packages.
Thousandths of a second. 200ms is one fifth of a second.
A command that moves or renames a file.
JSON with one item per line. Not a valid --output-format value; the real one is stream-json.
The tool that installs JavaScript packages and runs project scripts like npm test. npm i is short for npm install.
Runs a JavaScript package without installing it for good, e.g. npx prettier.
A standard way to log in to a service through your browser and grant an app access, without giving it your password.
Writing joined words with every word capitalized, like ProductList.
A system setting listing the folders where your computer looks for programs. A command works anywhere only if its program is in a PATH folder.
The installer for Python packages. It is not how you install Claude Code.
A faster alternative to npm that does the same job: installs packages and runs scripts.
The type of web request that sends data to a server, like submitting a login form. POST /login means 'send login details'.
A request on GitHub to merge your branch's changes into the main code, where teammates can review them first.
Lowercase spelling of PR, used in commands like gh pr create (open a pull request) and flags like --from-pr.
Plural of PR: requests on GitHub to merge changes after review.
Uppercase version of pwd. Commands are case-sensitive, so typing PWD fails; the command is pwd.
A command that shows which folder you are in right now.
The standard name for a project's introduction file (often README.md) that explains what the project is and how to use it.
A project folder tracked by git, with its full history of changes.
Plural of repo: git-tracked project folders.
A common style of web API where each address (like /users) is a thing you GET, POST, etc. to.
A command that deletes files permanently (no trash can). Be careful with it.
Amazon's cloud file storage. aws s3 ls lists stored files.
The folder that usually holds a project's source code.
An older way for a server to stream updates. As an MCP transport it is deprecated; use HTTP instead.
Lowercase value for --transport: the older remote MCP connection type, now deprecated. Use http instead.
A secure way to log in to another computer over the network. Not an MCP transport.
A separate output channel for error messages. Hook scripts write their reason for blocking here.
The channel a command reads its input from, such as text piped in with |.
An MCP transport where the server runs as a program on your own machine and Claude talks to it through its input and output.
The channel where a command writes its normal output.
A way of working where you write the tests first, watch them fail, then write code until they pass.
The last part of a web or email address, like .com or .org. 'a@b' has no TLD, so it is not a valid email.
Notes marking work still left to do.
With chmod: lets you (the file's owner, 'user') run the file as a program.
The part of an app you see and interact with: screens, buttons, menus.
A web address, like https://claude.ai.
Lowercase spelling of URL, a web address; used as a key in settings like "url": "https://...".
A pretend computer running inside a real one, kept separate so mistakes inside it can't harm your real files.
Plural of VM: isolated pretend computers running inside real ones.
Means 'compared with'.
Takes text arriving from a pipe and passes it to another command as arguments.
A plain-text settings format of key: value lines where indentation shows what belongs inside what. Used in frontmatter and GitHub workflows.
A compressed file that bundles several files into one smaller download.
Sends the output of the command on the left into the command on the right.
Short for your home folder, e.g. ~/.claude is the .claude folder in your home folder.
The start of a path inside your home folder, e.g. ~/projects.
